title: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
slides: Can a robot trust what it sees on screen?

thread_text:
1. Can a robot trust what it sees on screen?

Physicl just raised $10M to tackle that exact problem. The company builds digital worlds that are not simulated, meaning robots learn from real-world physics, not approximations.

2. Physicl raises $10M

The funding will accelerate the development of its non-simulated digital environments, where robots can safely fail and learn without expensive physical setups.

3. Real-world training gets cheaper

By using Physicl's digital worlds, robot training becomes faster and more cost-effective. Companies can test physical tasks without building multiple physical prototypes.

4. Test one physical task

Physicl invites you to try a single physical task this month. It's a hands-on way to see if their approach fits your needs.

5. Ready to try Physicl?

Sign up for a trial and test one physical task this month. If you don't, your competitors might beat you to it.
